extracted.intended_audience: Contracting Officers and procurement professionals (Navy / DOD) involved in Circular A-76 cost-comparison procurements
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative standards for conducting cost-comparisons, solicitations, evaluations, and awards under Circular A-76 / CITA procedures (Navy/DOD), including treatment of various contract types, disclosure rules, competition definitions, and solicitation methodologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of firm/bid offer procedure under Section 8(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: NAVMAT did not think the use of the firm/bid offer procedure was feasible under Section 8(a) procedures; DAR paragraph 1-705.5 provides that the use of an 8(a) set-aside does not necessarily constitute an award at the lowest price possible but only most likely costs under competitive conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using the firm/bid rule simultaneously with 8(a) solicitations; current guidance: C/I actions over $100,000 will be offered up for 8(a) and small business set-asides and firm/bid procedures will apply. SBA development monies will not be included in the cost comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: When cost comparison is complete and requirement for further solicitation
rubrics_metrics.description: If requirements were offered up for some type of set-aside, question of when the cost comparison process is considered complete and the Government in-house estimate revealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CNM guidance (Aug 1979): requirements processed under 8(a) require further solicitation under Small Business Restricted Advertising or unrestricted solicitation if the in-house cost estimate is lower than the 8(a) offer. Solicitations originally under competitive small business set-aside procedures would not require further solicitation if Government in-house cost estimate was lower.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure timing of Government in-house cost estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of an 8(a) set-aside, the Government estimate will be opened but not made public unless the cost comparison indicates the 8(a) offer is lower.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting Officer must advise SBA, the 8(a) offeror, and union representatives of this procedure. Standard clauses that provide copies of the in-house estimate 'upon request' at opening may be inconsistent with CNM guidance and should be reconciled with current policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of solicitation methodology (Two-Step vs. performance-oriented SOW)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-Step Formal Advertising may be appropriate under different circumstances but caused problems when requirements could have been clearly indicated in a performance oriented SOW and formally advertised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve Two-Step for large, complex, new starts (e.g., umbrella contracts). For conversions or where Government currently performs the function, use a clear, performance-oriented SOW and formal advertising to avoid issues like disputed minimum manning levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use contractor technical proposals to cover unclear specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Requesting contractor technical proposals should not be used as a crutch to offset the lack of clear and accurate specifications regarding performance of the desired service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft SOWs with performance standards and a surveillance plan so deductions for inferior performance can be based on established standards rather than proposal-provided manning or technical promises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of contractors not meeting proposed manning levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue arose where a contractor refused to provide the minimum manning levels indicated in his technical proposal submitted in step one; Contracting Officer withheld payment citing the Inspection of Services Clause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether contractor must man to proposed levels is a legal issue likely decided in court; avoid by writing clear SOWs and avoid reliance on proposal-stated manning as the basis for payment unless expressly required in contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and justification of incentive-type contract pricing arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of incentive type contracts for conversions necessitates the use of one of the 17 exceptions to Formal Advertising cited in DAR; difficult to justify that negotiated procurement was necessary because it would be less costly or impractical otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incentive arrangements are more applicable to large, complex, new starts rather than individual conversions; ensure strong justification and correct DAR exception if used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-priced out-year options to prevent buy-ins and base cost comparison period
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised Circular attempts to address buy-ins by indicating solicitations should provide for pre-priced options for out-year performance and the cost comparison would be based on a broader period (e.g., three years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh advantages (continuity, reduced turbulence) against DAR preference for resolicitation for annual requirements; recognize Service Contract Act implications which may limit cost-comparison to one year when SCA mandates redetermination of labor rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inflation assumptions for government labor costs in multi-year comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: As originally envisioned, government labor costs would be inflated for out years at the rate of 4% per year for a three-year comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given recent inflationary trends (e.g., 12% or more), the appropriateness of a 4% rate is questionable—reconsider escalation assumptions for accurate cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service Contract Act effect on length of cost-comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Service Contract Act mandates redetermination of labor rates for covered contractor employees, the cost comparison will be made for one year only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedure applies to solicitations released after October 1, 1979; continue to use three-year comparisons where SCA is not applicable and provide pre-priced options for out-years in those cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting Officer responsibility for conducting prebid/preproposal conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers will be responsible for conducting prebid/preproposal conferences and, in conjunction with the requiring activity, providing explanations of cost procedures to be applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COs must understand the procedures for calculating the Government in-house cost estimate and the methodology of comparison; explain cost differentials (conversion vs new start) and address contractor concerns such as bonds and use of existing personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and control of site visits and pre-award surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: Some contracting offices make site-visits in conjunction with pre-award surveys mandatory and require attendance of the contract negotiator even at distant locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting Officer should maintain control of site visits; avoid prospects conducting site visits or informal reviews without contracting office knowledge to preserve acquisition integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of informal communications to prevent unequal information
rubrics_metrics.description: Informal communications by prospective bidders or offerers without representation or knowledge of the contracting office may result in the prospective contractor receiving additional or contrary information not in the solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid such informal communications; ensure any substantive information is issued as an amendment so all bidders receive equal information and prevent unfair advantages or post-award disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain cost differential methods in preproposal memorandums
rubrics_metrics.description: Preproposal memorandums should explain in detail the cost differentials that will be used depending on whether the function is a conversion or a new start.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to explain these differentials can lead to incorrect expectations (e.g., erroneously stating that any lower contractor bid will automatically win rather than the correct conversion threshold such as 10% of Government personnel costs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat Government as another offeror for amendments/clarifications
rubrics_metrics.description: If solicitation amendments are required, the Government should be treated exactly as another offerer; procedures should include distribution of all amendments to the Task Group Chairperson and routing clarifications through the Task Group Chairperson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the Government in-house estimate is revised to reflect solicitation changes so the cost comparison remains valid and avoids 'apples and oranges' situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive amendments that invalidate the cost comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive changes, clarifications, amendments and similar items might result in the actual cost comparison being based on 'apples and oranges' situations between Government and contractor concepts of requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If many changes occur, assure the Government in-house cost estimate reflects these changes to preserve integrity of comparison; consider re-solicitation if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and conditions for price competition (DAR four conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: DAR states that in order for price competition to exist, four conditions must be met: (1) at least two responsible offerors, (2) who can satisfy the requirements, (3) independently contend for a contract to be awarded to the responsive, responsible offeror submitting the lowest evaluated price, (4) by submitting priced offers responsive to expressed requirements of the solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using this definition, the Government can be characterized as an offeror; assess competition accordingly when determining availability of private sources and applicability of reliance-on-private-sector exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination and entry of the 'contract price' on the cost-comparison form
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officer must enter the 'contract price' on line 10 of the cost comparison form; together with the Government in-house cost estimate this forms the basis for the actual cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different pricing arrangements require specific treatment: firm-fixed-price — enter low offer price (unclear if discounts included); fixed-price with EPA — handbook silent; FPIF — evaluate based on target price (not ceiling); other fixed-price variants — no definitive guidance; contracting officer must exercise judgment and consult guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of payment/early-payment discounts in evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost Comparison Handbook is silent as to whether payment discounts offered by the contractor should be included; discounts for early payment are used as an evaluation criteria and could be expected to reduce total Government costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations have been made to include payment discounts in the evaluation process so true lowest-cost to the Government is reflected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of cost-reimbursement (CPFF/CPIF) contracts and cost realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost Reimbursement Contracts must be subjected to meticulous technical and cost evaluation to assure estimated costs are neither over- nor under-estimated; Handbook emphasizes necessity for evaluating cost realism but is silent on what is entered on line 10 for CPFF/CPIF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request auditors to check offerors' estimates; for CPFF enter sum of total estimated costs and fixed fee; for CPIF use target cost combined with target fee (interviews indicated these practices), and negotiate upward price revisions if realism shows underestimation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) contracts in cost comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: For CPAF contracts the performance level comparable to that attributed to Government employees in preparing the Government estimate will be used to estimate the amount of the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of the appropriate portion of the award fee requires consultation with estimators and functional managers; Contracting Officer must make an informed, independent judgment to attribute fee commensurate with Government-equivalent performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Time-and-Material or Labor-Hour arrangements in comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: If Time and Material or Labor Hour type contracts are used, the Handbook indicates the total estimated cost of performance may be calculated and entered or, alternatively, comparable rates may be developed and the cost comparison conducted on the basis of rates rather than total costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either method may be used; research revealed little use of the rates-based method—COs should select the method that best reflects expected Government costs and document rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award factors vs evaluation factors — treatment of post-award government costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustments to reflect certain other costs to the Government that will be incurred only if a contract is awarded (transportation, contract administration, government-furnished materials/supplies, use of government-owned equipment/facilities, standby maintenance costs, Government personnel termination costs) are not evaluation factors in the true sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NAVMAT recommends these be treated as award factors because they: (1) are not used to determine an offeror's grasp of the requirement, (2) not used to evaluate expertise, (3) not used to differentiate or rank offerors, (4) not used in determining the competitive range, (5) not equally applied to all offerors, and (6) applied only to the otherwise successful bidder/offeror. Treat them in award phase similar to responsibility determinations and EEO compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling late submission of Government in-house cost estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing directives indicate the sealed in-house cost estimate must be submitted by the required submission date for bids and proposals, but no written guidance located on what the Contracting Officer should do if the cost estimate is submitted late.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some suggest automatic extension of solicitation, but that may unfairly favor Government. Contracting Officers should monitor submission closely, coordinate with task group, and extend bid opening prior to opening if necessary; current clauses may treat the in-house estimate as a 'proposal' subject to late-proposal rules which could imply rejection—resolve conflicts between CITA directives and solicitation provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public opening procedures for in-house estimate in negotiated solicitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Clause for negotiated solicitation stipulates that at conclusion of negotiation the Contracting Officer will set a time and place for public opening of the Government in-house estimate, notify interested parties, open and record the in-house cost estimate and provide a copy to interested personnel upon request; no contractor proposal information is to be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviewees indicated existing clause coverage is deficient; ensure public opening procedures are consistent with higher-level guidance and with whether the in-house estimate should be public at opening (formal advertising) or limited (8(a) treatments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for auditors and careful evaluation of offerors' cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews with OFPP personnel indicate auditors should be requested to check offerers' estimates to ensure they are neither unrealistically low nor too high.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use auditors to confirm cost realism; typical price negotiation develops a Government position lower than offered—upward price revisions to contractor offers may need to be negotiated to ensure equity in the cost comparison process.
